entities.summary:
Zoology is the scientific study of animals—their anatomy, physiology, behaviour, evolution, and classification—emerging as a distinct field within natural history and later biology. Classical authors such as Aristotle compiled systematic observations of animal life; early modern cabinets of curiosity and Linnaean taxonomy then professionalised zoology as a university and museum discipline across Europe.

Nineteenth-century evolutionary theory, field collecting empires, and laboratory physiology transformed zoology from descriptive natural history into experimental and comparative science. Colonial expeditions fed specimens into metropolitan museums even as ecology and ethology later recentred living animals in their environments.

Today zoology underpins conservation biology, veterinary science, and biodiversity assessment. As an idea and academic major it embodies the long effort to organise knowledge of animal life—and the political economies that funded that organisation.
